title: This Pagoda Looks 9 Floors — Secretly It's 17 | China Travel Expert
description:
This 900-year-old pagoda in Guangzhou looks nine storeys — but hides seventeen levels inside.

Liurong Temple dates back over 1,400 years. Its brick-and-wood Flower Pagoda was rebuilt in 1097, shows nine tiers outside but holds seventeen levels within, and once enshrined a thousand Buddha figures — earning it the name “Thousand-Buddha Pagoda.” In 1100 the poet Su Dongpo saw six banyan trees here and wrote “Six Banyans,” which became the temple’s name. It’s the tallest surviving Song-dynasty pagoda in Lingnan.

🧭 Expert Tip: Come right at opening — the nine glazed tiers catch dawn light and the courtyard is still empty.

一座塔，外看九层，内藏十七层——寺名还是苏东坡起的。
